steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' library to enable component creation and state management for cross-functional collaboration.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing core React features
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState, which are essential for building React components with state management.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement syntax. You need to import React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the main CollaborationDashboard component
steps.instruction: Create a functional React component named CollaborationDashboard that will serve as the main container for the application. Return null from the component for now.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. Make sure to export the component.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the CollaborationDashboard component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A CollaborationDashboard component is created and exported, ready to be the main container.
successCriteria: The CollaborationDashboard component is defined as a function that returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've established the main component structure for the collaboration dashboard.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named exactly 'CollaborationDashboard' and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check the name and that it returns null.

steps.title: Initialize state for team members
steps.instruction: Inside your CollaborationDashboard component, use the useState hook to initialize a state variable called 'teamMembers' with an array containing objects representing different functional roles (engineering, product, design, marketing).
steps.hint: Call useState with an initial array value. Each object in the array should have properties like 'role' and 'name' to represent team members from different functions.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a teamMembers state variable initialized with an array of objects representing cross-functional team members.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with an initial array containing at least one object for each functional role (engineering, product, design, marketing).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized state to manage cross-functional team member data. This is essential for tracking collaboration across different functions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your teamMembers state is initialized with an array of objects representing different functional roles (engineering, product, design, marketing).
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside the CollaborationDashboard component, use useState to create a 'teamMembers' state variable initialized with an array of objects for different functional roles.

steps.title: Initialize state for active collaboration
steps.instruction: Inside your CollaborationDashboard component, use useState to initialize a state variable called 'activeCollaboration' with a default value representing no active collaboration (e.g., null or an empty string).
steps.hint: Add a new useState call after your existing teamMembers state. The default value should indicate no collaboration is currently active.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing state for current task
const [currentTask, setCurrentTask] = useState(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have two state variables: teamMembers and activeCollaboration, both initialized with appropriate default values.
successCriteria: A state variable named 'activeCollaboration' is declared using useState with a default value representing no active collaboration.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized state to track active collaboration status. This will help manage which cross-functional collaboration is currently in focus.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've declared the state variable exactly as 'activeCollaboration' and given it a default value that represents no active collaboration.
steps.feedbackWrong: The activeCollaboration state wasn't properly initialized. Remember to use useState with the correct variable name and a default value that indicates no collaboration is active.

steps.title: Define handler to initiate collaboration
steps.instruction: Inside your CollaborationDashboard component, define a function called 'startCollaboration' that updates the 'activeCollaboration' state to indicate collaboration has begun.
steps.hint: Create a function that uses the setter from useState to change the activeCollaboration state value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a startCollaboration function that can be called to update the activeCollaboration state.
successCriteria: A function named startCollaboration is defined and uses the setter from useState to update activeCollaboration state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the startCollaboration function. This function simulates initiating cross-functional collaboration by updating the state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function is named exactly 'startCollaboration' and it updates the activeCollaboration state using the setter from useState.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Remember to create a function called 'startCollaboration' that updates the activeCollaboration state.

steps.title: Define handler to resolve collaboration issue
steps.instruction: Inside your CollaborationDashboard component, define a function called 'resolveIssue' that sets the 'activeCollaboration' state to null to simulate successful resolution.
steps.hint: Create a function that uses the setActiveCollaboration state setter to update the state to null.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a resolveIssue function that can be called to clear the active collaboration.
successCriteria: A function named 'resolveIssue' is defined inside the component and calls setActiveCollaboration with null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined a function to resolve collaboration issues, which is essential for managing cross-functional workflows.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function is named 'resolveIssue' and it updates the activeCollaboration state to null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The resolveIssue function is not correctly defined. Check that it's inside the component and properly updates the state.

steps.title: Create the main dashboard structure
steps.instruction: In your CollaborationDashboard component, return a container div with the CSS class 'dashboard-container' that will hold all dashboard elements.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement with a div element that has the specified class.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a div with the class 'dashboard-container' as the foundation for the collaboration dashboard layout.
successCriteria: The CollaborationDashboard component returns a div element with className='dashboard-container'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the foundational container for the collaboration dashboard. This provides the structure needed to organize team collaboration elements.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning a div element with exactly the class 'dashboard-container'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return a div element with className='dashboard-container' to create the dashboard structure.

steps.title: Display team member roles and status
steps.instruction: Inside your CollaborationDashboard component, map through the teamMembers state to display each member's role and collaboration status. Create a list where each item shows the member's name, role, and whether they are currently collaborating.
steps.hint: Use the map method on teamMembers to return JSX for each member. Display the name, role, and isCollaborating properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: A list of team members showing each member's name, role, and collaboration status appears in the dashboard.
successCriteria: The teamMembers state is mapped to display each member's name, role, and isCollaborating status in the UI.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully visualized the cross-functional team composition by displaying each member's role and collaboration status.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started mapping the team members, but make sure to display all three properties: name, role, and isCollaborating status for each member.
steps.feedbackWrong: The team members list isn't displaying correctly. Remember to use the map method on teamMembers and return JSX that shows each member's details.

steps.title: Add collaboration initiation button and wire handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside your component that calls the startCollaboration handler when clicked. The button should have text like 'Start Collaboration' and be styled with basic CSS.
steps.hint: Add a <button> element with an onClick attribute that calls startCollaboration with the appropriate argument. You can add inline styling like style={{ margin: '8px', padding: '8px' }}.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: button with handler
<button onClick={() => handleAction('task')} style={{ margin: '8px' }}>
  Perform Action
</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button element appears in the dashboard that, when clicked, will initiate collaboration for a team member by calling the startCollaboration handler.
successCriteria: Button element is present with text content
Button has onClick handler calling startCollaboration
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a button that can initiate cross-functional collaboration. This gives users direct control to start collaborative sessions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your button has an onClick handler that calls the startCollaboration function with appropriate arguments, and includes some basic styling.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button isn't properly configured. Remember to add a <button> element with onClick={...} that calls startCollaboration, and include some styling attributes.

steps.title: Add issue resolution button and wire handler
steps.instruction: Add a button inside your component's return statement that calls the resolveIssue handler when clicked, and conditionally display the current collaboration status.
steps.hint: Place the button after the team member list. Use the activeCollaboration state to show which member is currently collaborating.
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional button that resolves collaboration issues and displays the current collaboration status when active.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the issue resolution control and status display, completing the collaboration dashboard.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added both the resolution button and the conditional status display.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button or status display is missing. Review the instructions for adding the resolution control.
